correctness.rationale: On each cell the affine interpolation residual has the uniform expansion r_j(u)=-(h²/2) f''(a_j) z(u)+o(h²) with z=u(1-u), uniformly over all cells and u for f∈C². The z(U) distribution has cdf 1-sqrt(1-4t), mean 1/6 and variance 1/180. Fréchet–Hoeffding bound integrated over upper level sets shows the minimum covariance for two z-values with identical marginal law is at opposite quantiles. For U uniform, R=|2U-1| is uniform and the half-cell map T induces R↦1-R, so this optimal coupling is attained without changing either uniform marginal. Direct polynomial integrations give Var((z(U)+z(T(U)))/2)=1/2880, compared 1/360 independent and 1/180 for central U↦1-U. Independent cell pairs turn the leading h^6 cell contribution into global h^5 variance, with sharp limit ∫(f'')²/11520, comparisons /1440 and /720. Uniform interpolation o(h²) controls all coupling sequences. f=x² gives exact rates at every m. Independent rational polynomial checks corroborate these constants.
residual_risks: Only C², one dimension, equal cells, independent pairs across cells; uniqueness of an underlying uniform-coordinate copula is not asserted.

value.rationale: The estimator is a natural interpolatory stratified control variate whose residual is quadratic to first order and nonmonotone across its cell. Optimizing every two-marginal coupling at fixed evaluation cost is a meaningful sharp design problem; one-half/eighth/one-sixteenth variance constants quantitatively distinguish local reflection from central antithetics. Neither the reflection map nor countermonotone coupling theorem is itself claimed new. It does not purport to improve the global convergence order or optimize cross-cell correlations.
